title: Managed Environments: the Power Platform governance tier, its licensing condition and its controls
summary: Hold: the automation column confuses adding a group member with publishing rules, and an environment-specific digest control with an organisation-wide unsubscribe. The sharing-limit entry is instructions rather than runnable PowerShell, and Microsoft does document that a new group's rules are unconfigured.

claims.claim: Managed Environments provides premium governance capabilities for managing Power Platform at scale.
claims.quote: Managed environments are a suite of premium capabilities that allow admins to manage Power Platform at scale with more control, less effort, and more insights.

claims.claim: Managed environments can be used with any environment type.
claims.quote: Admins can use managed environments with any type of environment.

claims.claim: Administrators enable, disable and edit managed environments in the Power Platform admin center.
claims.quote: Admins enable, disable, and edit managed environments in the Power Platform admin center.

claims.claim: The non-exhaustive capability list includes environment groups, sharing limits, usage insights, data policies, maker welcome content, solution checker and IP Firewall.
claims.quote:
A managed environment encompasses, but isn't limited to, the following features:

- Environment groups
- Limit sharing
- Weekly usage insights
- Data policies
...
- Maker welcome content
- Solution checker
- IP Firewall

claims.claim: The data-policies capability provides a view filtered to policies applied to the managed environment.
claims.quote: The view is filtered to display only the data policies that are applied to the managed environment.

claims.claim: Maker guidelines is available only for managed environments.
claims.quote: Maker guidelines is available only for managed environments.

claims.claim: Maker guidelines is in preview.
claims.quote:
Configure maker guidelines for Copilot Studio (preview)

[This article is prerelease documentation and is subject to change.]

claims.claim: An environment group is a logical folder for environments.
claims.quote: Think of an environment group as a "folder" for your environments.

claims.claim: Environment groups can contain only managed environments.
claims.quote: Environment groups can only contain managed environments.

claims.claim: An environment can belong to only one group.
claims.quote: Each environment can belong to only one group, and groups can't overlap or be nested.

claims.claim: Environment groups cannot overlap.
claims.quote: Each environment can belong to only one group, and groups can't overlap or be nested.

claims.claim: Environment groups cannot be nested.
claims.quote: Each environment can belong to only one group, and groups can't overlap or be nested.

claims.where: What it is: Environment groups; Risks and limits
claims.claim: Published group rules are enforced in every member environment.
claims.quote: When a rule is published at the environment group level, it's enforced across every environment within that group.

claims.where: What it is: Environment groups; Risks and limits
claims.claim: Published group settings become read-only locally and cannot be overridden by local administrators.
claims.quote: This means the corresponding setting or policy becomes locked (read-only) within individual environments, ensuring that local system administrators can't modify or override these centrally defined rules.

claims.where: What it is: Environment groups; Open questions
claims.claim: Per-environment exceptions to published group rules are not currently supported.
claims.quote: Per-environment exceptions aren't currently supported.

claims.claim: Default environment routing can create a personal developer environment for a maker.
claims.quote: Instead of having new makers build in the shared Default environment, environment routing provisions a dedicated developer environment for each maker and optionally assigns it to an environment group of your choice.

claims.claim: Routing can place the new developer environment in a chosen group, already managed with that group's rules applied.
claims.quote: The environment comes preconfigured as a managed environment with all the group’s rules already applied from the start.

claims.where: What it is: Sharing limits; controls[1]
claims.claim: Sharing limits govern canvas apps, solution-aware cloud flows and agents.
claims.quote: If a user tries to share a canvas app, solution-aware cloud flow, or agent that contradicts the sharing rules, they're informed as shown.

claims.claim: Agent sharing rules control owners' and editors' ability to grant Editor permissions.
claims.quote: When selected: Owners and editors can share with any individual as an editor.When not selected: Owners and editors can't share with an individual as an editor.

claims.claim: Agent sharing rules control owners' and editors' ability to grant Viewer permissions.
claims.quote: When selected: Owners and editors can share with any individual as a viewer and any security group.

claims.claim: Agent sharing rules can exclude sharing with security groups.
claims.quote: If this setting is selected, owners and editors can only share with individuals as viewers. They can't share with a security group.

claims.claim: Agent sharing rules can limit how many viewers an agent is shared with.
claims.quote: If Only share with individuals (no security groups) is selected, you can control the maximum number of viewers with whom an agent can be shared with.

claims.where: What it is: Sharing limits; Risks and limits
claims.claim: Sharing rules are enforced when someone tries to share.
claims.quote: Sharing rules are enforced when users try to share an app, flow, or agent.

claims.where: What it is: Sharing limits; Risks and limits
claims.claim: Sharing rules do not remove access that existed before they were applied.
claims.quote: This restriction doesn't impact any existing users who already have access to the app, flow, or agent before the application of the sharing rules.

claims.claim: Group rules left untouched remain managed at the environment level.
claims.quote: Untouched rules are managed at the environment level.

claims.where: Why it matters; controls[1].note; Risks and limits
claims.claim: Agent sharing limits apply only to agents requiring authentication.
claims.quote: Sharing limits only apply to agents that require authentication.

claims.claim: Agent sharing controls can be configured per managed environment or through environment groups.
claims.quote: You can configure these controls for an individual Managed Environment, or you can apply the sharing controls at scale using Environment Groups and Rules in the Power Platform admin center.

claims.claim: The embedded-maker-credentials setting can restrict sharing of agents using maker-provided connections.
claims.quote: Administrators can use the Sharing agents with embedded maker credentials setting in the Power Platform admin center to prevent agents from being shared when they contain connections configured to use maker credentials that other users aren't permitted to reuse.

claims.claim: The embedded-maker-credentials control is documented as preview.
claims.quote: Control sharing agents with embedded maker credentials (preview)

claims.claim: Maker guidelines can be configured as an environment-group rule.
claims.quote: You can configure maker guidelines for an individual managed environment or for an environment group.

claims.claim: The embedded-maker-credentials control supports individual environments and environment groups.
claims.quote: You can configure the setting for an individual environment or an environment group.

claims.claim: The listed standalone Power Apps, Power Automate, Copilot Studio, Power Pages and Dynamics 365 licences include Managed Environments entitlement.
claims.quote: Power Apps Premium, Power Automate Premium, Microsoft Copilot Studio, Copilot Studio for Microsoft 365 Copilot (only for features related to Copilot Studio), Power Pages, Dynamics 365 Premium, Enterprise, Team Members, and Dynamics 365 Customer Insights.

claims.claim: Power Apps per app, Power Pages and Copilot Studio pay-as-you-go meters also qualify.
claims.quote: Pay-as-you-go meters for Power Apps per app, Power Pages, and Copilot Studio also qualify.

claims.claim: Activating Managed Environments makes qualifying standalone licensing or meters a condition of active usage.
claims.quote: When you activate managed environments in an environment, all active usage requires one of these standalone licenses or pay-as-you-go meters.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; What to check
claims.claim: Every user running an app is in scope, including users of standard apps, rather than only makers.
claims.quote: Every user who runs an app in a managed environment is in scope, including users who run standard apps. The requirement applies to active usage in the environment rather than to the type of app.

claims.claim: The Power Apps per app meter covers only Power Apps usage.
claims.quote: However, this meter covers Power Apps usage only; any Power Automate flow usage must be covered by standalone Power Automate licenses or Power Automate per flow plans.

claims.claim: Cloud flow usage needs Power Automate licences or per flow plans, without an in-context qualification.
claims.quote: Power Automate cloud flows that are triggered within apps or in context of apps or agents are covered by the respective Power Apps or Microsoft Copilot Studio standalone licenses.
claims.fix: Keep 'The Power Apps per app meter covers Power Apps usage only' and replace the remainder of that sentence with: 'Cloud flows triggered within apps or in context of apps or agents are covered by the respective Power Apps or Microsoft Copilot Studio standalone licences.' The same licensing page also says a Power Apps Premium or Power Automate Premium licence can satisfy the premium requirement for a user running both an app and a cloud flow; do not imply that every flow needs a separate Power Automate licence.

claims.claim: The Developer Plan does not include Managed Environments entitlement when users run their assets.
claims.quote: A managed environment isn't included as an entitlement in the Developer Plan when users run their assets.

claims.claim: Trial licences can license users subject to their restrictions, including the documented 30-day example.
claims.quote: Trial licenses can license your users in managed environments, but the restrictions specific to these types of licenses still apply. For example, trial licenses only license users for 30 days.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Risks and limits; What to check
claims.claim: Starting February 2027, users without an appropriate licence are blocked from opening apps in managed environments.
claims.quote: Starting February 2027, an appropriate license is strictly required for a user to open an app in a managed environment. If an appropriate license isn't assigned to the user, the app doesn't open

claims.claim: The licensing block does not remove apps from the environment.
claims.quote: Apps aren't removed from the environment, and access resumes after an appropriate license is detected.

claims.claim: App access resumes after an appropriate licence is detected.
claims.quote: Apps aren't removed from the environment, and access resumes after an appropriate license is detected.

claims.claim: An app, flow or agent out of compliance with sharing rules can only be unshared until compliant.
claims.quote: However, if an app, flow, or agent is out of compliance after rules are set, only unsharing is allowed until the app, flow, or agent is compliant with the new rules.

claims.claim: Sharing rules may take up to an hour to start being enforced.
claims.quote: After sharing rules are set in the Power Platform admin center, it may take up to an hour for them to start getting enforced.

claims.claim: Dataverse for Teams sharing rules do not affect publishing to the bound team but apply to sharing with other teams.
claims.quote: Sharing rules in Dataverse for Teams environments don't impact sharing to a Team when you select Publish to Teams. However, when a user attempts to share with individuals or groups in a Team other than the one bound to the environment, the sharing limits are enforced.

claims.claim: An environment removed from a group retains the last group configuration but its settings become unlocked.
claims.quote: When an environment is removed, it retains the last applied configuration from the group's rules but becomes unlocked, allowing a local admin to modify it going forward.

claims.claim: Joining a group can override local sharing, maker welcome, solution checker, usage insights, backup retention and generative AI settings.
claims.quote: If you've published any of the following rules within your environment group, the corresponding settings at the environment level are overridden when added to the group: sharing limits, maker welcome content, solution checker, usage insights, backup retention, and generative AI settings.

claims.where: Risks and limits; What to check
claims.claim: Unmanaged developer environments are deprecated and existing ones must have Managed Environments enabled before December 15, 2026 to be kept.
claims.quote: Unmanaged developer environments are deprecated. To keep an existing developer environment, enable Managed Environments on it before December 15, 2026.

claims.claim: Before disabling Managed Environments, administrators should ensure no managed capabilities are in use.
claims.quote: Before you disable managed environments, make sure none of the managed environments capabilities are in use.

claims.claim: Source and destination managed-environments properties must match for copy and restore operations.
claims.quote: The managed environments property must be the same in the source and destination before you can start to copy and restore environment lifecycle operations.

claims.where: Risks and limits; controls[5].note; What to check
claims.claim: Usage insights requires tenant-level analytics.
claims.quote: You must turn on tenant-level analytics to get usage insights.

claims.claim: Usage insights is unavailable in sovereign clouds including GCC, GCC High, DoD and China.
claims.quote: Currently, usage insights aren’t available in sovereign clouds, such as Government Community Cloud (GCC), Government Community Cloud – High (GCC High), Department of Defense (DoD), and Power Platform and Dynamics 365 services in China.

claims.claim: Enable or edit managed environments under Manage > Environments > environment ellipsis > Enable Managed Environments or Edit Managed Environments > Enable or Save.
claims.quote:
Select the ellipsis next to an environment, and then in the menu, select Enable Managed Environments. If the environment is already managed, select Edit Managed Environments.
4. Configure the settings, and then select Enable or Save.

claims.claim: Set-AdminPowerAppEnvironmentGovernanceConfiguration with EnvironmentName and UpdatedGovernanceConfiguration containing protectionLevel Standard enables management.
claims.quote:
protectionLevel = "Standard"
...
Set-AdminPowerAppEnvironmentGovernanceConfiguration -EnvironmentName <EnvironmentID> -UpdatedGovernanceConfiguration $GovernanceConfiguration

claims.claim: Setting protectionLevel to Basic removes the managed-environments property.
Enabling or editing management requires Power Platform Administrator or Dynamics 365 Administrator in Microsoft Entra ID.
claims.quote: To enable or edit managed environments, you need the Power Platform Administrator or Dynamics 365 Administrator role in Microsoft Entra ID.

claims.claim: Sharing rules are under Manage > Environments > managed environment > Edit Managed Environments > Manage sharing.
claims.quote:
On the Environments page, select a managed environment.
5. In the command bar, Edit Managed Environments.
6. The sharing rules are located in the Manage sharing section.

claims.claim: The printed 'Set bot-limitSharingMode ... then Set-AdminPowerAppEnvironmentGovernanceConfiguration' entry is a runnable PowerShell call after replacing placeholders.
claims.quote: Searched: Set-AdminPowerAppEnvironmentGovernanceConfiguration bot-limitSharingMode Get-AdminPowerAppEnvironment. Opened managed-environment-sharing-limits: it documents Add-Member and saving a configuration, not the printed natural-language 'Set ... then' expression.
claims.fix: Replace the natural-language call with: '$environment = Get-AdminPowerAppEnvironment -EnvironmentName <EnvironmentId>; $governanceConfiguration = $environment.Internal.properties.governanceConfiguration; $governanceConfiguration.settings.extendedSettings | Add-Member -MemberType NoteProperty -Name "bot-limitSharingMode" -Value "ExcludeSharingToSecurityGroups" -Force; Set-AdminPowerAppEnvironmentGovernanceConfiguration -EnvironmentName <EnvironmentId> -UpdatedGovernanceConfiguration $governanceConfiguration'. Keep the existing documentation URL. State in the note that this example prevents agent sharing with security groups rather than configuring every app, flow and agent rule.

claims.claim: Group rules are configured through Manage > Environment groups > group > Rules > rule > Save > Publish rules.
claims.quote:
Select a rule to open its configuration panel. Adjust it as needed, then Save the rule. Repeat this step for all the rules you want to configure in this group.
7. Select the Publish rules button in the command bar.
claims.fix: Keep the cited path, but add: 'Microsoft also documents the rules-gallery experience using + Add rules and Apply rather than Publish rules.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/environment-group-rules-gallery, whose Rule lifecycle section describes that different experience.

claims.claim: The add-environment-to-group CLI call is the automation counterpart of configuring and publishing environment-group rules.
claims.quote:
pac environment-management add-environment-to-group

(Preview) Add the environment to the environment group.
claims.fix: Retain the valid command and its --group-id and --environment arguments, but change this row's governs text to 'Environment-group rules and membership' and add to its note: 'The UI configures and publishes rules; the CLI example only adds an environment to the group and does not configure or publish rules.' Change the table lead's 'the script, API or command that does the same' to 'the documented automation, with any difference in operation or scope stated in the note'. Apply these changes in both front matter and the rendered table.

claims.where: controls[2].note; Governance controls; What to check
claims.claim: A Power Platform tenant administrator configures group rules, and only published rules are enforced.
claims.quote: After you create the environment group, Power Platform tenant administrators can immediately add managed environments or configure the group's rules. Both approaches work, but keep in mind that only published rules are enforced across environments.

claims.claim: The credential-sharing control is under Security > Threat detection > Sharing agent with embedded maker credentials > Environments or Environment groups > Set up > Save.
claims.quote:
Environment groups: In the Environment groups tab, select the environment group for which you want to configure the setting.
- Environments: In the Environments tab, select the environment for which you want to configure the setting.
5. Select Set up.
claims.fix: Insert 'select the environment or environment group' after the tab choice. The pre-check's missing phrase is not a nonexistent tab: both tabs are documented separately. Also note that https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/configure-sharing-agents-embedded-maker-credentials documents the alternative path 'Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Features > Sharing agents with embedded maker credentials', with All sharing allowed and Safe sharing enforced modes, rather than the cited preview page's allow/block options.

claims.claim: No PowerShell or API control for the embedded-maker-credentials setting is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: embedded maker credentials PowerShell API; embedded maker credentials Set-Organization API pac. Opened the security/control-sharing-agents-with-embedded-maker-credentials, admin-sharing-controls-limits and configure-sharing-agents-embedded-maker-credentials articles; no setting call found.

claims.claim: Maker guidelines is configured at Copilot > Settings > Maker guidelines > Environments > environment > Edit setting.
claims.quote: Environment: Select Copilot > Settings, and then select Maker guidelines. Select the Environments tab, select the environment, and then select Edit setting.

claims.claim: No PowerShell, Graph or Power Platform API control for maker guidelines is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: maker guidelines PowerShell API; maker guidelines Power Platform API Dataverse; maker guidelines pac Set-AdminPowerAppEnvironmentGovernanceConfiguration. Opened maker-guidelines; read pac admin set-governance-config reference excerpt; no maker-guidelines operation found.

claims.claim: The environment's digest inclusion checkbox is under Manage > Environments > managed environment > Edit Managed Environments > Usage insights.
claims.quote: On the command bar, select Edit Managed Environments, select the settings under Usage insights, and then select Include insights for this environment in the weekly email digest.

claims.claim: Setting disableAdminDigest to True and saving tenant settings is the automation counterpart of the environment-specific digest checkbox.
claims.quote: Here's an example PowerShell script that unsubscribes your entire organization from the weekly digest.
claims.fix: Replace this row's API with kind 'pac-cli', call 'pac admin set-governance-config --environment <environment-id> --protection-level Standard --exclude-analysis', and docs 'https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/developer/cli/reference/admin#pac-admin-set-governance-config'. Replace the tenant-unsubscribe note with: 'The CLI example excludes this environment from the weekly digest.' That reference explicitly documents --exclude-analysis as excluding usage insights for the environment. The existing note correctly identifies the current script's tenant scope, but does not make it an equivalent environment control.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented which rules are enabled by default in a new environment group.
claims.quote: At this point, the group is empty (contains no environments) and none of its rules are configured.
claims.fix: Replace this question and 'Not yet documented' answer with: 'A new environment group is empty and none of its rules are configured.' The existing cited environment-groups page states this in Create an environment group.

claims.claim: The checklist's instruction to run the licensing report is represented in the controls table.
claims.quote: Checklist: 'Run the Users requiring licenses in Managed Environments report before February 2027.' Governance notes: 'Two more surfaces have no row above.' The table has no licensing-report row.
claims.fix: The licensing-report checklist step has no corresponding controls-table row. Remove this checklist bullet; retain the documented report guidance in Governance controls. No additional row is required by this correction.

claims.claim: The checklist's instruction to check the tenant-level analytics control is represented in the controls table.
claims.quote: Checklist: 'Check who receives the weekly digest and that tenant-level analytics is on.' The digest row says 'Needs tenant-level analytics' but provides only the environment digest checkbox and tenant digest opt-out, not the analytics control.
claims.fix: Remove 'and that tenant-level analytics is on' from this checklist bullet; retain the verified analytics prerequisite in Risks and limits and the digest row's note. No additional row is required by this correction.

claims.claim: Delegated Admin and Environment Admin cannot change the managed-environments property.
claims.quote: Users with the Delegated Admin role or the Environment Admin security role can't change the managed environments property in an environment.

claims.claim: The weekly digest is sent to Power Platform administrators and Dynamics 365 service administrators.
claims.quote: The weekly digest is sent to all users with the roles of Power Platform administrator and Dynamics 365 service administrator.

claims.claim: Additional recipients can be added to the digest.
claims.quote: To add more recipients, select Add additional recipients for the weekly email digest, and then select Weekly digest. Enter email addresses in the Additional recipients box.

claims.claim: Managed environments excluded from reporting are omitted from the digest.
claims.quote: The weekly digest provides insights into all managed environments in your tenant that you haven't excluded from reporting.

claims.claim: No weekly digest is sent if all managed environments are excluded.
claims.quote: If you exclude all your managed environments, Power Platform won't send a weekly digest.

claims.claim: Usage insights gives administrators weekly information about apps, makers and usage.
claims.quote: Analytics about your top apps, your most impactful makers, and inactive resources you can safely clean up are distilled and delivered to your mailbox once a week.

claims.claim: Editing a managed environment exposes Data policies > See active data policies for this environment.
claims.quote:
Edit the selected managed environment's settings.
5. In the Data policies section, select See active data policies for this environment.

claims.claim: The Users requiring licenses in Managed Environments report is downloaded through Licensing > Power Apps > Summary > Download report.
claims.quote:
In the Summary tab, select Download report. The Download license information pane appears.
5. From the Usage type list, select Users requiring licenses in Managed Environments.

claims.claim: Environment routing can be reached through Manage > Environment groups > Environment Routing.
claims.quote:
Select Manage in the navigation pane.
2. In the Manage pane, select Environment groups.
3. Select the Environment Routing button in the command bar.

claims.claim: Maker guidelines displays an administrator message, optional link and contact information in the Copilot Studio Review pane.
claims.quote: When a maker selects Review for an agent in Copilot Studio, the pane shows the agent's blockers and warnings together with A message from your admin. The maker can use the configured link or email without leaving the Review experience.

claims.claim: The pac environment-management commands are in preview.
claims.quote: (Preview) Manage environment lifecycle, governance, DR, SKU, and environment groups.

claims.where: What to check: republishing group rules
claims.claim: Changed group rules are marked until published and must be republished to apply their changes.
claims.quote: Updated rules appear in bold with an asterisk (\*) until published. Remember to republish rules to apply changes across environments.

claims.claim: The licensing page describes the February 2027 block in terms of opening apps.
claims.quote: License required to open an app: Starting February 2027, users who don't have an appropriate license are blocked from opening apps in the managed environment after receiving the final notification stage.
